Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Shared turret acceptance

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Run nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turret/run.sh from the repository root. REPLAY_TURRET_OUT optionally selects a fresh absolute output directory; otherwise the suite retains an isolated temporary project and logs. It builds native Godot scripts and checks the full scripts package for WASM, runs seven pure tests and a native/WASM takeover corpus, exercises the authored workbench, then runs host/client/spectator and three-member occupied host-crash scenarios.

The real-peer fixture uses 120 ms configured latency, admits normal ability and mount/release actions, rejects an occupied claim, hands remaining ammo to another player, and requires empty-turret cleanup plus matching complete world hashes. Spectators must drain the scene at their observed clock; occupancy disappears at the authoritative final shot. The crash fixture waits for a backup that contains the occupied turret before killing only its own original host process.

fixtures/content50.checkpoint is a genuine tick-12 content-50/J checkpoint, captured before live types changed (local reservation token bytes start with 77). The conversion test decodes it with frozen types and verifies all mapped state, an empty turret pool and zero new definition fields. Do not regenerate it with current codecs. The frozen catalog/action source and schemas live under examples/replay_scrapyard/shared/revisions/content50.

See feature documentation and recorded evidence.
